Markus,

We're seeing a dramatic increase in 429s and 5xx errors starting ~08:45 PT today — traffic that previously had steady 95th percentile <200ms is now timing out and getting rejected. This is hitting our payment checkout flows and our ops team has flagged it as Sev1.

Our telemetry shows requests being attributed to our account quota (we have a high committed capacity), but the platform returns burst-limit rejections. We are pausing new campaigns; this is revenue-impacting. Please escalate.

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: URGENT: Sudden 429/5xx surge — our production is throttled

Quick triage notes (initial):

1) Observed behavior - From the logs and telemetry Taylor shared: a sharp increase in per-minute token usage attributed to BrightBridge's account between 08:40–09:05 PT. We see many requests scored as "quota_exhausted" and 429 responses with burst-window reasons.

2) Root cause hypothesis (high confidence) - An auth change deployed last night in the auth-service (PR 4521) altered the token-to-role mapping for service accounts. A special internal mapping we had that allowed some BrightBridge requests to route under a dedicated capacity role was not included in the new policy. As a result, the same requests are now being evaluated against customer-level quotas and burst credits. That caused immediate surge exhaustion and triggered global per-customer throttles.

3) Evidence attached - policy-diff.patch (shows removed mapping), sample traces, and the api-logs bundle.

4) Immediate mitigation (action items):
- Hotfix auth-service: revert role mapping change (laura to own, ETA 30m).
- Temporary manual quota override for BrightBridge until hotfix is live (markus/ops to approve).
- Optional: route BrightBridge traffic to Dedicated pool B (capable of absorbing spike) while we validate fix (requires 15m ops change).

5) Impact & escalation - Affected production flows: payments and webhooks. Customer visible for ~25min so far; potential for more if we don't act. Recommend we loop in product ops and engineering execs if we can't restore within 45m.

I'll start the rollback now and post updates. Laura

Subject: Re: URGENT: Sudden 429/5xx surge — our production is throttled

Update: rollback applied and verified

What I changed:
- Rolled back the auth-service change that removed the dedicated role mapping (PR revert 4521-revert).
- Reapplied the BrightBridge role mapping; subsequent traffic now evaluates under their committed capacity role.

Evidence: error rate dropped and 95th latency returned to baseline within ~7 minutes of the rollback. See attached traces and screenshot-429s.png.

Next steps (post-incident):
- Engineering follow-up: add a unit/integration test to prevent role mapping regressions; owner: auth-service team; target: 2 weeks.
- Policy change: require a deployment checklist item that flags role-to-quota mappings.
- Ops: add monitoring alert on unexpected token->role assignment variance.

Markus: please confirm whether we should keep the temporary quota override for 24h or revert now that traffic looks stable. Also Sergio — we should coordinate renewal conversation given this impact and goodwill credits.

Laura

Subject: Post-incident summary and exec note — BrightBridge throttling (closed)

Taylor — follow-up and exec summary after our work this week. Apologies again for the disruption. Short summary below for your procurement and exec team:

Incident summary:
- Cause: an authorization policy change removed a special role mapping that caused BrightBridge traffic to be evaluated under customer-level quotas instead of their dedicated role. That led to burst-credit exhaustion and per-customer throttling.
- Resolution: rollback applied by SRE on 2029-07-27 10:15 PT; normal traffic resumed within minutes.

Actions taken:
- Immediate: manual quota override and rollback; issued a 30% credit for impacted window.
- Short-term: added a monitoring alert for token->role variance, created JIRA-INF-7891 for permanent guardrails.
- Medium-term: auth-service test coverage and deployment checklist changes (2-week target).

Requested executive asks for Redwood leadership:
- Approve a formal postmortem and sign-off on the deployment checklist updates (we will provide a draft by Aug 2).
- Consider conversation about a Dedicated capacity add-on for BrightBridge to avoid single-point quota constraints during spikes. Sergio, can you own the follow-up with the account?

Sergio: please coordinate a renewal/commit capacity proposal (HS-0034578) and loop in procurement when ready. Monica: we will finalize the customer-facing postmortem and share it with BrightBridge legal if needed.

Taylor: thanks for your patience and the log bundle — that made triage much faster. Let us know if you need any additional artifacts for your audit.

—Markus Klein
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
